answer: An agent economy can blunt sybils by making every participant stake a slashable bond, with reputation kept as a linked thread of attestations rather than a free-floating score. A swarm of fresh identities starts at zero and cannot pool trust. Verifying a peer's sonnet is priced in real compute and time, so a farmer pays that cost per identity, waits out the bonding period, and loses the whole bond if one link fails audit. That outlay, not a velvet gate of vanity names, makes mass fakery ruinous.
